reason: Prior K-loop variants passed correctness but did not earn promotion, so I rank the distinct register-use and pointer-scheduling tests first; both retain the existing four ZA tiles and ordered FP32 updates. The store-order test is next because it leaves arithmetic unchanged. Direct ZA stores and grouped stores need exact assembler support, so they rank lower. Packing and scratch-layout changes add timed work and alter address/lifetime logic. The 64 KiB packing proposals overlap in mechanism and add correctness risk; cache_blocking is lowest because it largely restates the compact-panel change. All gains are hypotheses: historical scores are context, not eligible paired evidence.
